papers.title: TRIB3 Knockdown Attenuates Post-cardiac Arrest Brain Injury with Suppression of Mitophagy: Involvement of AKT-FOXO3a-BNIP3 Signaling.
papers.summary: This study looks at brain injury following cardiac arrest and resuscitation, focusing on a protein called TRIB3 that appears to be involved in the damage process. The researchers found that reducing TRIB3 levels lessened brain injury, and this effect was linked to decreased mitophagy, the process of clearing out damaged mitochondria. They identify a signaling pathway involving AKT, FOXO3a, and BNIP3 as the mechanism connecting TRIB3 to this mitophagy regulation.
papers.why: This paper offers direct mechanistic insight into mitophagy regulation in neurons during brain injury, which is central to the PhD project's focus on mitophagy and autophagy pathways in neuronal health and disease.

papers.title: Spatial mTOR biology: From organelle localization to biomolecular condensates and metabolic control.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how mTOR signaling is organized in space within cells, including its localization on organelles like lysosomes and its organization into biomolecular condensates. It discusses how this spatial arrangement controls metabolic signaling outputs, linking subcellular compartmentalization to functional regulation of growth and catabolic pathways. The abstract suggests a broad conceptual synthesis rather than new experimental data on a specific tissue type.
papers.why: mTOR is a central regulator of autophagy and mitophagy, so understanding its spatial organization could inform how autophagic flux is locally controlled in neuronal compartments relevant to this PhD project.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Protein Quality Control as a Hierarchical Defense System in Health and Disease.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how mitochondria maintain healthy proteins through a tiered defense system that includes molecular chaperones, proteases, and ultimately mitophagy when damage is too severe to repair. It frames these quality control mechanisms as working in a hierarchical manner, starting with molecular-level fixes and escalating to whole-organelle removal. The review likely discusses how failures at any level of this hierarchy contribute to disease, particularly neurodegeneration.
papers.why: Understanding the full hierarchy of mitochondrial quality control, from chaperones to mitophagy, provides essential mechanistic context for interpreting mitophagy dysfunction in neurons and how it may intersect with interneuron vulnerability and perineuronal net integrity.

papers.title: Exercise to Enhance Mitophagy in Parkinson's Disease - A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review discusses how physical exercise may help clear damaged mitochondria from brain cells through a process called mitophagy in people with Parkinson's disease. It likely summarizes evidence from animal and human studies showing exercise boosts mitochondrial quality control pathways. The review probably proposes mechanisms by which exercise-induced mitophagy could slow neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
papers.why: This review is relevant because it addresses mitophagy regulation in neurons, a core mechanistic focus of the PhD project even though it does not directly involve spatial omics or AI methods.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Quality Control and Apoptotic Thresholds in Major Depressive Disorder: A Structured Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This paper is a structured narrative review examining how mitochondrial quality control mechanisms, including mitophagy, relate to apoptotic thresholds in major depressive disorder. It synthesizes existing literature on mitochondrial dysfunction as a contributor to neuronal stress and depression pathology. No new experimental data is presented, as the focus is on reviewing and organizing current conceptual understanding.
papers.why: This review could provide useful background on how disrupted mitophagy and mitochondrial quality control link to neuronal vulnerability, which may inform interpretation of mitochondrial health markers in your spatial transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses of neurons.

papers.title: Identification and initial characterization of proteins involved in post-fertilization sperm mitophagy.
papers.summary: This paper investigates proteins that mediate mitophagy, the selective clearance of mitochondria, occurring in embryos after fertilization to eliminate paternal sperm mitochondria. The authors identify candidate proteins and provide initial functional characterization of their roles in this post-fertilization mitochondrial clearance process. The work focuses on reproductive biology and early embryonic mitochondrial quality control rather than neural tissue.
papers.why: Although this study examines mitophagy in a reproductive rather than neural context, it may offer mechanistic insights into mitophagy pathway components and regulatory proteins that could inform understanding of analogous mitochondrial quality control processes in neurons.

papers.title: The role of SIRT3 in abdominal aortic aneurysm via regulating the PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy pathway.
papers.summary: This study examines abdominal aortic aneurysm, a vascular disease involving weakening of the aorta's wall. It investigates how the protein SIRT3 influences this condition by controlling PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, the process cells use to clear damaged mitochondria. The findings suggest that SIRT3 activity, by regulating this mitochondrial quality control pathway, affects aneurysm development or progression.
papers.why: Although focused on vascular tissue rather than brain, this paper is relevant because it details molecular mechanisms of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, a core pathway directly applicable to studying mitophagy dysfunction in neurons.
